approved_by: study owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3 (2026-10-06): revision-2 rule (aligned evidence is not automatically mandatory) approved; eight needs-review decisions and 14 flagged-item repairs applied; approval recorded after contract/rules/audit consistency and leak checks

functional_semantics.triton: out[dest_loc[t], h, d] = kv[t, h, d] for both tensor pairs via flat offset decomposition + index load + store (impl_triton.py L32-42); returns (out_nope, out_rope) (L91).
functional_semantics.cutile: Same semantics via gather of dest_loc[token] + ct.scatter (impl_cutile.py L49-61); returns (out_nope, out_rope) (L135).
functional_semantics.note: Both match impl_torch.py L25-26 (index_copy_ along dim 0 into a clone of o_*). dest_loc is a permutation (tensors.py L151), so every row is overwritten and writes never collide.

stages.triton: Two launches of one kernel: nope (L89) then rope (L90), each a 1-D grid over the flattened element count (L61-76).
stages.cutile: Two launches of one kernel: nope (L124-127) then rope (L130-133), each a 1-D grid over the flattened element count.
stages.note: Identical structure; the two scatter-copies are independent and may be fused into one launch (contract permits).

dependencies.triton: nope and rope launches touch disjoint buffers; both require the output buffers obtained from _cached_out (L87-88).
dependencies.note: No dependency between the two copies; both depend on the output buffers being initialised from o_* (see preprocessing).

reduction_scan_sort.triton: None; plain store at computed destination, no atomics, no collision handling (L42).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: None; ct.scatter with unique destinations, no atomics (L61).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Unique destinations by construction of the generator; neither side resolves duplicates.

precision.triton: Exact element copy for fp16/bf16/fp32/int8 (L41-42); dest index narrowed int64 -> int32 (L38).
precision.cutile: Exact element copy (L59-61); dest index narrowed to int32 (L55).
precision.note: No arithmetic on values; both narrow the index identically.

preprocessing.triton: out_nope/out_rope = clone of o_nope/o_rope created on the FIRST call per input tensor identity and cached in a module-level WeakTensorKeyDictionary (L7, L10-15, L87-88); later calls reuse the buffer, so the clone (allocation + device copy of both o_* tensors) is outside the steady-state timed window.
preprocessing.cutile: Identical pattern (L24, L27-32, L75-76) plus metadata-only .contiguous().view(-1) flattening (L80-83).
preprocessing.note: Both sides (and impl_torch.py L4-12) agree with each other. Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): the task domain fixes dest_loc as a permutation of all rows (tensors.py L151 torch.randperm; comment L149-150), so every output row is overwritten and the copy of o_* into the output is not a required stage (permitted mapping; device work counted when performed). Result values must never be carried across calls; an output allocation may be reused only when the call fully overwrites every result element; writing into o_* stays forbidden. Both manual sides satisfy this: the per-identity buffer is rewritten in full by the scatter on every call and no output value survives from an earlier call.

intermediate_storage.triton: No scratch; the persistent output buffers are the only module-level state (L7).
intermediate_storage.cutile: No scratch; same persistent output buffers (L24).
intermediate_storage.note: Both agree; the persistence question is recorded under preprocessing/mutation.

mutation.triton: No positional input is written (kv_*, dest_loc, o_* read-only); the cached output buffers are overwritten in place on every call (L42, L87-90).
mutation.cutile: Same: inputs read-only, cached outputs overwritten in place (L61, L75-76, L124-133).
mutation.note: Agreed: inputs are never modified and the outputs must not alias any input. Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): the returned tensors may be the same allocation across calls only because the scatter overwrites every element on each call (dest_loc is a permutation); no result value may be reused across calls. Rows not named by dest_loc do not occur in the fixed task domain.

fq_boundary.note: n = total_tokens * (kv_nope_head_num*kv_nope_head_dim + kv_rope_head_num*kv_rope_head_dim) (tensors.py infer_problem_size L652-656). Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): Q = n * dtype_size * 2 (one read of kv and one write of out per element) is the compulsory source-read + result-write lower bound of the scatter-copy and stays the formal denominator; the dest_loc index reads (8 B per token, re-gathered per element) are lower-order and remain omitted; no candidate-specific initialisation traffic term is added, so an implementation that copies o_* into its outputs pays that device copy inside the timed window against the same Q. The manual references launch exactly the scatter per call (the per-identity clone happens once, before steady state), so their timed work equals the Q traffic.

review_items: Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): output-buffer policy. dest_loc is a permutation of all rows in the benchmark domain (tensors.py L151 torch.randperm, comment L149-150), so every output row is overwritten by the scatter; a separate copy of o_nope/o_rope into the outputs is not a mandatory logical stage (permitted as a mapping, counted when performed). Outputs must be correct for the current call and must not alias inputs; no cached output values or result reuse across calls; an allocation may be reused only if the call fully overwrites every result element before return. The scatter-copy algorithm and the no-collision guarantee are kept.

Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): bytes_expr stays n * dtype_size * 2 (compulsory source read + result write); index traffic is documented as omitted/lower-order; no candidate-specific initialisation term is added. human_reference_comparable set to true: the manual references' per-call device work is exactly the scatter.

Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): rows not addressed by dest_loc do not exist in the fixed task domain (permutation); the evaluator verifies the permutation case only and does not test a non-permutation dest_loc.
